text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Islamist Welfare Party plans to increase media restrictions gradually through the introduction of new regulations.
- Seventeen people, mostly Ukrainian women, die in a fire which broke out at a hotel in central Istanbul.
- Sedat Bucak, a deputy seriously injured in a car crash which killed a gangster and a police chief, is reported to have gone to France for treatment.
- Former president Kenan Evren says he could return to politics if forced to do so by the conditions in the country .
- Some 200 bureaucrats in the Minister of Culture, run by the Islamist wing of the coalition, are moved to the southeast and religious school graduates are appointed in their place.
- An Islamist proposal to open overland travel for those making the Moslem pilgrimage to Mecca is rejected by the Interior and Foreign Ministries due to security reasons.
- Some 10,000 students from Turkic republics in Central Asia have been educated in Turkey since 1992.
- The government expects revenues of $20 billion from a third economic package expected to be unveiled on Tuesday.
- The editor of more than sixty pornographic publications faces a record jail sentence.
